newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel shares extend gains on Q1 sales.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel shares extend gains on Q1 sales.

text.p: Shares in Alcatel Alsthom SA extended early gains on the back of a 12.1 percent rise in first quarter sales which Alcatel chairman Serge Tchuruk said showed the company was on the road to recovery.

Alcatel shares climbed as much as 5.58 percent, hitting a high of 681 francs, the largest gain among CAC-40 shares. They were trading at 678 francs, up 5.12 percent at in volume of 715,347 shares at 1052 GMT, outpacing a 1.34 percent increase in the CAC-40 index of blue chip stocks.

Alcatel and privately-held Dassault Industries also said on Tuesday they had rejected an offer from Germany's Daimler Benz Aerospace (DASA) for an alliance similar to one DASA has concluded with Lagardere's Matra in its rival bid for Thomson-CSF.
The companies told a joint news conference they would start talks with DASA if their offer to buy the French government's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF were approved.

They said they had agreed to start talks with Britain's GEC with a view to creating a European joint venture integrating part of the companies' defence electronics activities if the joint Alcatel/Dassault offer for Thomson were accepted.
